literal: At the time the royal enterprise was newly founded; claws and heart, the close and trusted, were mostly kin appointed—only Li alone was sent far, and he was not a relative by marriage.
idiomatic: The realm was newly forged; intimates were kin—only Li was posted far away, no marriage tie to the throne.

literal: He had repeated battle merit and was appointed General of the Left Army.
idiomatic: Repeated merit made him General of the Left Army.

literal: Li's nature was blunt and careless, proud of favor, and he did not observe ritual propriety.
idiomatic: Li was blunt and proud of favor and scorned ritual.

literal: Before Daowu he stretched himself insolently without self-restraint, laughing and spitting as he pleased.
idiomatic: Before Daowu he lounged insolent, laughing and spitting at will.

literal: Daowu seized on his old offenses and executed him.
idiomatic: Daowu seized his old offenses and executed him.

literal: Thereupon majesty first grew stern; restraining the court to full humility began with Li.
idiomatic: From Li onward majesty grew stern and the court learned humility.

literal: Xi Juan, a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Xi Juan was from Dai.

literal: In youth he had military stratagem.
idiomatic: In youth he had military stratagem.

literal: In Daowu's reign he had battle merit.
idiomatic: Under Daowu he won battle merit.

literal: In Mingyuan's time he was garrison commander of Wulao, and raiders feared him.
idiomatic: Under Mingyuan he held Wulao; raiders feared him.

literal: In Taiwu's time he was enfeoffed Duke of Nanyang.
idiomatic: Under Taiwu he was made Duke of Nanyang.

literal: On the campaign against the Rouran, Juan as Director of the Capital Bureau supervised detached generals on a separate route.
idiomatic: Campaigning against the Rouran, Juan as Director of the Capital Bureau led detached columns on a separate road.

literal: An edict ordered a rendezvous at Luhun Sea; Juan, Prince of Zhongshan Chen, and the other great generals were all late; he was beheaded south of the capital and his title abolished.
idiomatic: Ordered to meet at Luhun Sea, Juan, Prince of Zhongshan Chen, and other great generals were all late; he was beheaded south of the capital and his title struck.

literal: Discussion says: The rise of emperors, though heaven's mandate, in what the classics teach all rely on worthy arms.
idiomatic: The commentators say: Emperors rise by heaven's mandate, yet every classic teaches they lean on worthy arms.

literal: In the days of Emperor Shenyuan and Emperors Huan and Mu the royal trace was not yet bright; in the season when Cao and Han raced to establish themselves, they made their own ground of merit—men of resolve and insight indeed.
idiomatic: In the age of Shenyuan and Huan and Mu the throne was still dim; in the rush of founding, men of resolve carved their own merit.

literal: Yet the brothers Liu Kuren took loyalty as heart and did not waver in rise or fall.
idiomatic: Yet Liu Kuren and his brother held loyalty through rise and fall.

literal: The purity they kept looked far ahead; yet both met untimely death—pity!
idiomatic: Their purity aimed far; both died untimely—pity!

literal: The brothers Wei Zhen were loyal and brave, rousing themselves, righteousness making them forget life.
idiomatic: Wei Zhen and his brothers were loyal and brave, righteousness making them forget life.

literal: Juan's martial renown stood in his age and enlarged the family estate.
idiomatic: Juan's renown in arms enlarged his house.

literal: Mu Chong long served the dragon countenance, early showing sincere devotion, and therefore received favor to the summit of the secretariat.
idiomatic: Mu Chong long served the throne, showed early loyalty, and rose to the secretariat's peak.

literal: He even took part in treasonous plotting yet in the end was wholly spared and shared sacrifice in the temple—this too honored merit.
idiomatic: He even joined treason yet was spared and shared the temple rites—merit still counted.

literal: Generation after generation of dukes and ministers, rank on rank of purple and blue—how grand!
idiomatic: Generation on generation of ministers in purple and blue—how grand!

literal: Xi Jin for generations was called loyal and filial; in campaigns he had victories.
idiomatic: Xi Jin was called loyal and filial for generations and won his battles.

literal: In the Pingliang campaign the army was destroyed and he was taken captive; though the blame of defeat at Yao was pardoned and the rite of returning the corpse was not achieved, favor and rites were still lavish and he was sacrificed in the temple hall.
idiomatic: At Pingliang his army was lost and he was captured; though Yao's blame was pardoned and his corpse never came home, rites and favor were lavish and he was honored in the temple.

literal: Shu Sun Jian in youth showed sincere diligence and in the end achieved service; on the frontier he had method, his might shaking Yi and Chu.
idiomatic: Shu Sun Jian showed early loyalty and earned lasting service; on the frontier his method shook Yi and Chu.

literal: Jun held to his pledge under Mingyuan, righteousness shining in hardship; discerning the change at Zhuti, he had the air of Jin Midi—added to softness that could correct, he was praised in court and countryside.
idiomatic: Jun kept faith under Mingyuan in hardship; reading Zhuti's change, he had Jin Midi's spirit—soft yet upright, praised in court and field.

literal: An Tong, a man of another stock, yet his wisdom entered use and his appointment matched the age's best—there was reason indeed!
idiomatic: An Tong, of alien stock, yet his wit was used and his rank matched the age's best—no accident!

literal: Ji captured He Lian Chang and broke the Song hosts—he became a famed general not lightly matched.
idiomatic: Ji seized He Lian Chang and broke Song's armies—a general not lightly matched.

literal: Yu Yeyan is recorded for peril and for service in the founding hour; wisdom and courage both shown, merit and name both raised—yet he could not escape ruin; that too was his fate.
idiomatic: Yu Yeyan shone in peril and founding; wit and courage, merit and name—yet ruin took him; fate, perhaps.

literal: Wang Jian's rank and favor were already high; he sought uprightness by denunciation—in the affair of Canhe, was it not his crime?
idiomatic: Wang Jian stood high; he sought uprightness by accusation—at Canhe, was the crime not his?

literal: Luo Jie's branch clung to the trunk; sons and grandsons enjoyed rank and stipend.
idiomatic: Luo Jie's line clung to power; sons and grandsons fed on rank.

literal: Lou Fulian and Lu Dafei both won fame campaigning in Dai and left their names to earlier ages.
idiomatic: Lou Fulian and Lu Dafei both won fame in Dai and left names to earlier ages.

literal: Xi Mu, He Ba, Mo Ti, He Digan, Li Li, and Xi Juan had loyal, diligent merit in campaign yet could not humble themselves before merit and fame—all came to execution; each had his fate.
idiomatic: Xi Mu, He Ba, Mo Ti, He Digan, Li Li, and Xi Juan served loyally in war yet would not bow before fame—all were executed; each had his fate.
